_doc: One entry per slash alternation printed in Wakelin et al. (1958).
These slashes are TRANSCRIBER UNCERTAINTY, not alternatives the speaker
offered, so POL-027 (one S block per option) does not automatically apply.
mode=variant  a clear spelling variant - mostly overlapping letters and
the same gloss. Published as FORM[@kindOf="alternate"]
siblings on the node that varies, and on its ancestors.
mode=split    everything else. Published as separate S blocks; the first
keeps the printed sentence number, the rest take letter
suffixes b, c, ... (POL-037 forbids renumbering the
`carriers` names the snapshot node holding FORM[@kindOf="alternate"].
Rows marked review=true are the borderline calls - see README.

decisions.note: both glossed 'name-we'. The recorded alternate 'namen-em' drops 'ngaran'; it is probably 'ngaran-namen-em'. See the source-discrepancy report.

MAINTAINER CORRECTION to the source (2026-09-07), not a reading of it: the article's last two glosses are in the wrong order, and the slash divides the word rather than one morpheme inside it. The corrected gloss 'unan-many-still/again-them' divides at its own slash exactly where the text does, giving 3+3 and 2+2. See README, 'A correction to the source'.

decisions.note: MAINTAINER RULING (2026-09-07): the article's optional-material parentheses here mark an alternation, `kan` ~ `kan-u`, so the word carries an alternate FORM like a slash case. The S FORM keeps the printed `kan(u)` notation (POL-017); the alternation is resolved on the word. This row carries no slash, so nothing is rewritten above the W.
the two readings have different glosses ('kill-with-boiling-water' vs 'if-not-killed-with-boiling-water'), so they are different clauses, not spellings
a single-vowel alternation in a function word; both glossed 'unan'. Treated as a spelling variant even though 'a' and 'u' share no letters - the alternation is one vowel, not one word.
two different lexemes with different glosses; 'nitelemna' carries no source segmentation

two different lexemes sharing one gloss. Neither is segmented in the text, so the gloss is a single two-word unit written 'bamboo.strips' in Leipzig dot notation (maintainer correction, 2026-09-07); it was 'bamboo-strips', which reads as two morphemes.
l ~ r in the same stem, same gloss
one word vs a three-word phrase. Published as S48 + S48b, which is the shape already published; the snapshot no longer pre-materializes S48b (it also carried a malformed W id, S4bW2).
pure hyphenation variant - the clearest spelling-variant case in the corpus. The snapshot now keeps the printed slash like every other alternation, so this needs no special handling.
